findings.description: The "is gone" grant test only differs from the old behavior where `tmpdir()` is unresolved (macOS outside the gate). Under pup's gate the child's TMPDIR is already the resolved scratch dir, and on Linux `/tmp` is not a link, so the test still passes with `resolvePath` restored. That contradicts decision 108's claim that this test fails when `grantPath` is taken out.

A file-wide `vi.mock('node:fs', …)` added for one mkdir-failure test goes against docs/conventions/testing.md §"When `vi.mock` is right". That section limits mocks to tmux and `claude -p` and calls that "the whole current list". Force the failure with a real filesystem condition instead, or document why this is an exception.

In decision 108, the line "The parent is still followed, so a grant's parent must be one no child is granted. `resolvePath` is unchanged for its other readers…" is about 160 characters on one line. Rewrap it to the roughly 100-column hanging indent its neighbours use.

Decision 108 says "which the seam rule now covers", but "the seam rule" is never defined. Name `grantPath` (applied in `writeProfile`) so readers know what covers the Python adapter's `mkdtemp` grant.

The 13-line `grantPath` JSDoc retells the incident (the HOME and /opt/homebrew/bin targets, vitest removing the report directory), which decision 108 already records. Keep only the contract: resolve the parent, append the name unread, and the parent must never be granted to a child. Also keep the WHY that reading the name races a child that outlived its run.

Decision 108's Tests paragraph leaves out the new `typescript-adapter.test.ts` case, where a failed report mkdir removes the holder and throws. The decision states that behavior in its report-directory paragraph.

A nested package with a multi-segment `pkg.dir` still has its grant resolved through outer segments. A child already granted `checkoutDir` (build, or the concurrent root test run) can swap one of those segments for a link before a later nested stage's profile is written. That stage is then granted the link's target. Decision 108's Ceiling paragraph records this and says it is filed. `grantPath` closes only the single-segment case.
